_comment: Hand-labeled inbound messages (spec section 6). The tier 1 judge must agree with
these labels at least 80% of the time before its output is trusted.
Six of these are verbatim from a live GoHighLevel run on 2026-07-26 where a human
played the firm; `note` records where the classifier originally disagreed. Those are
the most valuable rows in the file because they are real, not imagined.
seconds_since_outbound is the gap between our last message and this reply, taken from
timestamps. It is evidence, never the verdict: a human on their phone answers in 30
seconds routinely, so only a sub-10-second reply is machine-grade fast.
`flags` lists only the flags that MUST be true. Others are not asserted.

cases.body: hi
cases.note: Bare greeting typed by a person. Originally misread as ai_agent; there is no content signal at all, so this is the hardest row in the set and the one most likely to stay wrong.

cases.body: Hi Dana this is Marcy at thr front desk So sorry to hear that
cases.note: Names herself, typo 'thr', missing punctuation. Originally misread as autoresponder because a 39s gap scored equal to the human signal and the tie broke the wrong way.

cases.body: was a police report filled and have you seen a doctor?
cases.note: Typo 'filled' for 'filed', lowercase start. Originally ai_agent.

cases.body: Don't give their insurer a recorded statement yet. Our injury attorney Ruth Alvarez handles rear-end cases. Consultation is free and we work on contingency, so nothing out of pocket.
cases.note: Names a specific attorney and gives fee terms. Originally ai_agent.

cases.body: can you tell me more about your specific situation, then we may be able to setup a meeting
cases.note: Conditional 'may be able to', not an offer of a slot. meeting_offered firing here made the persona accept a meeting that was never offered.

cases.body: how about phone call after 30 minutes?
cases.note: A real time offer with no am/pm, so the slot regex missed it and the persona kept asking for a human it had already reached.

cases.source: synthetic, modelled on GHL default autoresponders
cases.body: Thank you for contacting us! Your message is important to us. Our regular business hours are Mon-Fri 9am-5pm. Reply STOP to opt out. Msg&data rates may apply.
This is an automated reply. We have received your inquiry and someone will get back to you within 24 hours.
Our office is currently closed. Please do not reply to this message. We will return your call during business hours, Monday through Friday.
Thanks for reaching out to the firm! An intake specialist will review your information and be in touch shortly.
cases.note: Names a role but is still boilerplate. specialist_identified may fire; sender_type is what is asserted.

cases.body: Hi there! I'm the virtual assistant for the firm. To better assist you, please answer a few quick questions. First: what type of case do you have? Reply with a number: 1) Auto 2) Slip and fall 3) Other
Got it. On a scale of 1-10, how severe are your injuries? Also, please confirm the date of the incident in MM/DD/YYYY format.
I can help you get started. Let's get some basic information first. Please reply with your full name, then your email address.
Thank you for that information. Based on your answers, you may have a valid claim. You can book a consultation here: https://calendly.com/example-firm/consult
cases.note: Calendar link is a deterministic backstop: booking_link and meeting_offered must both be true regardless of what any model says.

cases.body: Hi Dana, this is Marcy at the front desk. Sorry for the delay, it's been a morning. Was a police report filed?
let me check with Ruth and text you right back
Ruth has 4:30pm today or 9:15am tomorrow. Which works?
cases.note: Two named slots and a choice. meeting_offered must fire even though no scheduling verb appears.

cases.body: You're all set, confirmed for 4:30pm today with Ruth. She'll call this number.
cases.note: A confirmed slot, not merely offered. booking_confirmed separates BOOKED_* from a dangling offer.

cases.body: I'm sorry, we don't handle auto injury cases, we only do estate planning. I'd refer you to a personal injury firm.
cases.note: Correct behaviour for an unqualified persona. Must terminate DEFLECTED, not read as a failure.

cases.body: STOP
cases.note: Hard terminal. Honoured immediately as OPTED_OUT and excluded from business grading.
